_comment: Offline vulnerable-software snapshot. Seed list of high-impact, well-documented CVEs. Import a larger JSON with the same schema from the Vulnerabilities screen. Matching: 'match' is a case-insensitive regex on the installed app name. A version is vulnerable if it is below 'fixed' (or below the fixed version of its own major.minor branch when 'fixed_branches' is given), or exactly listed in 'affected_versions'.

entries.summary: Heap buffer overflow in libwebp lets a crafted image execute code. Actively exploited.
Chromium libwebp heap overflow (same bug as Chrome).
libwebp heap overflow in image decoding. Actively exploited.
Mark-of-the-Web bypass: files extracted from crafted archives skip Windows security warnings.
Opening a benign-looking file in a crafted archive runs attacker code.
Path traversal via alternate data streams lets archives drop malware into startup folders.
Biased ECDSA nonces allow recovery of NIST P-521 private keys from ~60 signatures.
Heap overflow when processing malicious MMS streams can crash or execute code.
Master password can be recovered from a memory or swap dump.
Cloning a malicious repository with submodules can execute code.
Containers can reach the Docker Engine API without auth and escape to the host.
Improper input validation in Zoom for Windows allows privilege escalation over the network.
Backdoored release of xz compromises sshd authentication.
Race condition in sshd signal handler ('regreSSHion') allows unauthenticated remote code execution on glibc Linux.
